name: Identity Decoy (AD Services Trap)
description: Emulates Windows identity services (LDAP, LDAPS, RDP) so intruders enumerating or authenticating against them are detected and their usernames and credentials recorded.

documentation.summary: The Identity Decoy answers like a domain controller: it serves LDAP/LDAPS directory binds and accepts RDP connections, then reports every authentication attempt, including NTLM binds from tools such as BloodHound.py, impacket and SharpHound. It targets the lateral-movement phase, where an attacker tries directory enumeration (ldapsearch, BloodHound) and credential reuse against RDP. Captured passwords are stored as a keyed hash by default, never in cleartext.

sections.title: Features
content: Shared persona: LDAP, LDAPS and RDP all present one hostname and AD domain, so the decoy looks like a single real machine.
Credential capture: LDAP simple-bind credentials and the RDP mstshash username are recorded; passwords are stored as a keyed HMAC by default (TS_CAPTURE_PASSWORDS).
Believable replies: a bad LDAP bind returns an AD-style 'data 52e' error, and the RDP connection confirm uses the handshake bytes a real Windows host returns.
In-memory TLS: LDAPS generates its certificate at startup, so nothing is written to the read-only filesystem.

sections.title: Security Architecture
content: Global Sandbox Baseline: Enforced by the TrueSignal Hub. Drops ALL default Linux kernel capabilities and enforces a read-only filesystem.
Execution Privilege: Runs as container root (UID 0) strictly to bind low-numbered ports (389, 636).
Required Capabilities: Adds 'NET_BIND_SERVICE' to bind ports below 1024 without full host network control.
Data Handling: Captured passwords are HMAC-hashed by default; cleartext ('plain') is opt-in and should stay out of PCI scope.

heuristics.recommendation_reason: Directory or remote-desktop services detected. Deploy the Identity Decoy to catch Active Directory enumeration, password spraying and RDP credential reuse during lateral movement.

env_vars.name: TS_HUB_ENDPOINT
env_vars.description: The URL of your central TrueSignal Hub.

env_vars.name: TS_SENSOR_ID
env_vars.description: Unique identifier for this specific trap.

env_vars.name: TS_SEVERITY
env_vars.description: Fallback alert severity (the sensor sets critical for logins, low for bare connections, medium for queries).

env_vars.name: TS_SERVICES
env_vars.description: Comma-separated services to run, as proto:port (proto is ldap, ldaps or rdp). Standard ports keep the decoy believable.

env_vars.name: TS_PERSONA_HOSTNAME
env_vars.description: Hostname the decoy claims (e.g. the fake DC name).

env_vars.name: TS_PERSONA_DOMAIN
env_vars.description: Active Directory domain the decoy claims.

env_vars.name: TS_CAPTURE_PASSWORDS
env_vars.description: How captured passwords are recorded: hash (keyed HMAC-SHA256 + length, default), plain (cleartext; avoid in PCI scope), none.

env_vars.name: TS_CAPTURE_NTLM
env_vars.description: NTLM capture for RDP NLA and LDAP/LDAPS NTLM binds (Sicily and SASL GSS-SPNEGO): identity (default, record DOMAIN\\user + workstation), hash (also record the crackable NetNTLMv2; for threat intel, avoid in PCI scope), off (RDP mstshash cookie only; LDAP refuses NTLM with authMethodNotSupported).

env_vars.name: TS_CAPTURE_HASH_KEY
env_vars.description: Set by the Hub: this node's capture key (derived from the Hub's master key), so password HMACs can be matched against planted honeytokens. Any value set here is ignored.
